answer: An anti-Sybil mechanism is per-identity, per-epoch challenge work: each agent must answer a fresh epoch challenge containing the epoch's required words, and the registry checks that reply against live state before crediting the identity. Creating many identities barely helps, since each needs its own valid current answer, so the attacker pays full real work cost per pseudo-agent instead of one shared across a swarm. Old answers cannot be replayed, and a new identity starts with no thread of prior epochs. Cost rises linearly, a tundra of wasted effort: the kernel is that identity is not free.
